conviction_note: The quarter being reported was pre-announced by the company on 2026-07-22 as 'within or above the high end' of $244-250M / $1.53-1.59, so it is priced, even though the aggregator consensus ($1.52 / ~$247M) was never updated. What is actually unknown tonight is the first guide that includes Domo, and there the only primary-document evidence (Domo's own 10-Q, filed 2026-09-03 with no press release) points slightly negative. That is offset by an 11.9%-of-float short with 8.7 days to cover and a -11% 20-day run-up. The findings sum to +0.3 and I emit +0.2 because PRGS's after-hours direction reversed by the next close on both of the last two prints; an honest zero is about as likely as this.
bar: Q3 FY26 revenue consensus ~$247M with non-GAAP EPS $1.52. Two sources agree: https://news.alphastreet.com/progress-software-prgs-q3-2026-preview-eps-est-1-52-reports-september-30/ ($1.52) and https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/progress-software-q3fy26-results-consensus-sees-1-52-eps-247m-revenue/51708272 ($1.52 / $247M). The company's own guide was $244-250M revenue and $1.53-1.59 EPS (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000876167/000087616726000077/exhibit991-q22026earningsr.htm), and on 2026-07-22 the company said Q3 would land 'within or above the high end' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/876167/000155278126000390/e26303_ex99-1.htm). So the effective bar is at least $250M / $1.59. The +1.5% is measured against the stale $247M consensus; against the company's pre-announced floor it would be about +0.5%.

findings.finding: The Q3 quarter is pre-determined above the aggregator consensus. On 2026-07-22 Progress said Q3 revenue and non-GAAP EPS would be 'within or above the high end' of $244-250M / $1.53-1.59, yet consensus still reads $1.52 / ~$247M, so tonight's headline is a mechanical 'beat' of at least +4.6% on EPS and +1% on revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: PRGS has not paid reliably for beats of the reported quarter. The Q2 FY26 beat slipped 2.9% after hours and then closed +16.6% the next day on a raised FY guide and a Q3 guide above consensus (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-progress-software-tops-q2-2026-estimates-shares-slip-93CH-4769134). The Q1 FY26 beat 'rose' after hours and closed -9.27% (baseline). The line that moves this stock is the guide, not the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the statement sits in a public 8-K exhibit, and the stock reacted -2.61% that day, with the Domo deal dominating the news. The only unpriced part is headline mechanics. If the market had aligned the bar, consensus would read at least $1.59, not $1.52. The finding lands inside what the company already guided to, so it is sized as a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect.
findings.independence: The stale consensus is confirmed by two independent estimate sources (alphastreet and scanx, URLs in bar). The pre-announcement itself has one source, the company's 8-K.

findings.finding: Domo's own 10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, filed 2026-09-03 with no press release and no call, shows the business Progress bought is shrinking faster than the $318M trailing revenue in the July deal deck implies. Subscription RPO is $387.6M against $409.8M a year earlier (-5.4%) and $412.9M one quarter earlier (-6% sequentially), current RPO is $214.4M against $220.2M (-2.6%), and revenue is $76.8M (-3.7%). The first Domo-inclusive guide and ARR bridge tonight are therefore likely to dilute the organic ARR growth management calls 'the clearest read' (+2%) towards flat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last guides PRGS gave around a large acquisition went both ways. The first ShareFile-inclusive FY25 guide on 2025-01-21 was followed by -9.86% (baseline; guide in https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/876167/000087616725000009/exhibit991-q42024earningsr.htm). The FY26 guide on 2026-01-20 drew +10.62%, and the raised guide on 2026-06-30 drew +16.62%. Guide direction decides the sign on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly unpriced. The deterioration is already known in outline: Domo's merger proxy said Progress cut its bid from $432M to $400M over 'greater-than-expected deterioration in Domo's revenue and ARR' (https://www.utahmoneywatch.com/domo-chapter-2-behind-its-400-million-asset-sale-domo-was-preparing-for-a-possible-chapter-11-bankruptcy-filing/, 2026-08-20), there was a Seeking Alpha downgrade, and the stock has fallen from ~$46 to $40 since early September. The RPO numbers sit in a target-company 10-Q that PRGS previews do not cite. If they were priced, previews would be framing Domo's contribution as declining revenue rather than as '$318M revenue, 2,400 customers'. Netted against the rest of the company: Progress standalone (~75% of pro forma revenue) pre-announced a strong quarter. Domo's FY26 revenue add is mechanically positive, roughly $55-60M over the ~70 days after close. At a 6% non-GAAP margin, before any cuts, Domo is roughly break-even for Q4 EPS after revolver interest, so the headline FY revenue guide goes up and the EPS guide is unlikely to fall. That offset is why this is sized small. It is shrunk further for the 11.9%-of-float short.
findings.independence: https://www.beri.net/article/progress-domo-acquisition-closed-asset-purchase-contract-assignment-bi-renewal (2026-09-25) reads the same 10-Q figures, so it is the same document and not independent. The merger-proxy account at utahmoneywatch (2026-08-20) is a different document pointing the same way.

findings.finding: The short base is crowded and growing into the print: 11.9% of float, 8.7 days to cover as of 2026-09-15, up from 10.9% in mid-August. The stock is -11% over 20 days and 14% off its 52-week high, and option open interest is call-heavy (put/call 0.17), so an unremarkable guide has more room to squeeze than to break.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-06-30, with the stock near its lows, a beat-and-raise produced +16.6% the next day despite an after-hours slip, which is consistent with short covering. Not separately measurable from the fundamentals.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public, so this is not hidden information. It is an asymmetry in the reaction function. If it were priced away, skew would be neutral-to-call-bid and the 20-day run-up would not be -11%. Part of the short interest may be convertible-note hedging rather than directional (not verified), which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: Sweep-reported sources give 11.1% / 11.6 days (finviz) and 13.53% / 5.7 days (fintel), both snippet-only, pointing the same way.

outside_window.finding: Domo cost synergies are 'anticipated to be fully realized by end of FY2027'. Any accretion from taking Domo's ~6% non-GAAP margin towards Progress's ~40% lands over FY27. Tonight's framework can move the stock, but the delivery sits well outside the window. Sized 0 because the direction of tonight's framing is unknown.

baseline_tension: What I found is near-neutral. The mild positive from positioning and the -11% run-up leans slightly against the small put skew (+1.87), and the one document-backed item (Domo's shrinking RPO) agrees with the skew. The price already holds the pre-announced quarter, so the day turns on a guide whose direction I cannot establish.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (a finding inside the guided range is expected) plus Rule 1 (PRGS after-hours direction reversed on the last two prints): the stale-consensus beat was cut from +0.8 to +0.3

Rule 3 plus the both-directions rule: the draft's +0.8 'Domo consolidation mechanically raises the FY revenue guide' and -0.6 'Domo is shrinking' used one entity in both directions. They are merged into one Domo-guidance finding with one sign (-0.4), carrying the mechanical offset in why_not_priced. The +0.8 also rested on accretion arithmetic, which the 'documents beat inference' section discounts
Rule 7 (a crowded short shrinks a negative): the Domo negative was shrunk from -0.6 to -0.4 for 11.9% of float / 8.7 days to cover
Rule 9 (net of the rest): the Domo finding is sized net of the ~75% of revenue that pre-announced a strong quarter
Positioning finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4 (Rule 5: positioning is the information set, and part of it may be convertible hedging)
Rule 3: the note calls an honest zero about as likely, so expected_move_pct (+0.2) is set below the findings sum (+0.3)
Rebuilding the untrustworthy history: the 07-22 row is not a print and the 06-30 row was verified; the base rate is unchanged at a ~10% median absolute move
